script: I exposed the creep—snorting baking soda ruined his internet reputation forever.. The first time I met my ex‑girlfriend, we were both in the middle of a 1999 HTML chat called "The Attic." The chat was a wild, unfiltered place where anyone could whisper nasty stuff into your private screen. The only defense was a separate community we built on a free website, where we'd list creeps and flood them with Ctrl+V whispers until they quit. My girlfriend was a legend there—tough, creative, and supposedly "more evil than the devil." (I'll get to that later.) Then came Farmer‑Bob. He slipped into our group as a "new" user, claiming he owned a cattle farm and was rich. He bragged about wooden shoes and how "females" adored him. We didn't trust him, so we let him think he was one of us. He was clueless, obviously, but we needed proof. So my girlfriend pretended to be naive and flirtatious, demanding cocaine for a hookup. He fell for it, saying he couldn't afford it and that his parents were out of town. Classic bait‑and‑switch, right? Next, she dropped the bomb: "Hey Farmer‑Bob, you know mixing three parts baking soda with one part vanilla sugar gives a cocaine‑like rush? It's cheaper, too!" I thought he'd see through it, but he was like, "I forgot about that DIY cocaine trick! Thanks for the reminder." She convinced him he had to make a batch before her train ticket, and he promised to try it that night. A couple of days later, an email in all caps hit us: "YOU MADE MY NOSE BLEED, YOU MF BCH! I HAD TO VISIT A CLINIC BECAUSE OF YOU!!!" He was furious, accusing her of tricking him. But that was just the start. We escalated. We claimed she ran a side gig producing German amateur spanking porn, using a homemade "nose candy" for the "rush." To prove it, we recorded a ridiculous fake trailer. My girlfriend's younger brother pretended to be her, and another friend sat on his lap, both wearing ridiculous costumes. With a wooden spatula and a shaky camera, we filmed a slap‑and‑spank scene, complete with German‑sounding nonsense. The video was so low‑quality it looked convincingly fake. Farmer‑Bob, convinced we were genuine, begged us for the film. We said, "Only if you try the homemade cocaine again." We never heard from him again. He probably kept creeping under a new name, but no more emails from him. (The trailer's hard drive died, but that's the story.) That's how we turned a creepy internet creep into a laughingstock. And honestly, I am still better at this than anyone else who's ever tried to out‑creep a creep.
